title: Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023
text:
PARUAWeSt UNDARY COMMISSION BILL, 2023
Li B R ■

—**“ MEMORANDUM

The object of the Bill is to establish the Ghana Boundary Commission
to determine and demarcate the land boundaries of Ghana and delimit
the maritime boundaries of Ghana in accordance with accepted principles
of international law and to protect and secure the interest of the Republic.

The Ghana Boundary Commission Act, 2010 (Act 795) was passed
by Parliament and assented to by the President on 22nd April, 2010.
Act 795 in its current form does not adequately reflect best practice in
international and internal boundary architecture. Act 795 does not include
some contemporary functions of the Commission as compared to
international best practice. The current functions of the Commission are
woefully inadequate and do not cover key areas for an integrated response
to boundary disputes. There are also major omissions in the constitution
of the governing body of the Commission. Key Ministers such as the
Ministers responsible for the Interior and National Security are absent.

Furthermore, the Act does not also provide for the creation of the
office of the Commissioner General of the Ghana Boundary Commission
in line with similar institutions in the country. In addition, the Act fails
to provide for the establishment of Departments of the Commission and
regional offices for the efficient and effective implementation of the
functions of the Commission. Also, detailed financial provisions are not
provided for in Act 795 which is hampering the implementation of the
functions of the Commission.

The lines of reportage between the Commission, Ministries,
Departments and Agencies necessitate a holistic review to ensure clear
channels of reportage. The required changes to Act 795 necessitate a repeal
of the Act and the enactment of a new comprehensive piece of legislation
to adequately respond to emerging national and international boundary
challenges and cater for the strategic direction in handling boundary
disputes.

In this regard, the Bill seeks to provide for the expansion of the
governing Board and the functions of the Commission based on
international best practice and considering Ghana’s national security

GHANA BOUNDARY COMMISSION BILL, 2023

architecture. The Bill expands the existing role of the Commission to
include the appropriate measures to deal with any boundary dispute that
affects the territorial sovereignty of Ghana or that may arise within the
country with a view to settling the disputes, promote trans-border
cooperation and border community development, and formulate policies
and implement programmes on international boundaries, specifically land
and maritime boundaries.

The Bill also provides clear guidelines on the channels of reportage.
In this regard, two technical committees namely, the Land Boundary
Technical Committee and the Maritime Boundary Technical Committee
are to be established. These committees have the Commissioner-General
as the chairperson with membership drawn from the relevant State agencies
and other stakeholders.

Administratively, the Bill seeks to provide for the establishment of
the office of the Commissioner-General. The Bill also provides for the
creation of five Departments, each to be headed by a Director and the
establishment of satellite regional offices of the Commission where
required. In addition, the Bill provides for the appointment of other staff
of the Commission and the establishment of an Internal Audit Unit in
accordance with the Public Financial Management Act, 2016 (Act 921).
Provision has also been made for funding of the activities and programmes
of the Commission.

Ultimately, the Bill seeks to repeal the Ghana Boundary Commission
Act, 2010 (Act 795) to establish the required national structures to address
emerging boundary challenges and to take cognisance of other significant
matters not catered for in Act 795.

Clause 1 establishes the Ghana Boundary Commission as a body
corporate. The objects of the Commission as specified in clause 2 include
undertaking negotiations to determine and demarcate the land boundaries
of Ghana and delimiting the maritime boundaries of Ghana in
accordance with accepted principles of international law in collaboration

ii

GHANA BOUNDARY COMMISSION BILL, 2023

with the Lands Commission, protecting and securing the interest of the
Republic in determining and demarcating land boundaries and delimiting
maritime boundaries of Ghana and adopting international best practice
in the demarcation of land boundaries and delimiting of maritime
boundaries of Ghana, among others.

Clause 3 provides for the functions of the Commission. These include
negotiating with a neighbouring country concerning a land boundary,
maritime boundary or air boundary between Ghana and that country; in
collaboration with relevant security agencies, ensure the security of the
boundaries of Ghana to safeguard the territorial sovereignty of Ghana
at all times; in collaboration with the Lands Commission, undertaking
the physical demarcation and survey of land boundaries and the
delimitation of maritime boundaries and whenever determined by the
Board, placing of buoys or other maritime markers along some or all of
the courses of the maritime boundaries of Ghana. Other functions of
the Commission include advising Government on the most appropriate
strategy for the negotiation of a land boundary or maritime boundary;
advising Government on international Conventions in relation to the
borders of Ghana and the signing and ratification of treaties related to
land and maritime boundaries; addressing issues related to the use of
natural resources that straddle land boundaries and maritime boundaries;
and formulating policies and implementing programmes on international
boundaries specifically land and maritime boundaries.

In clause 4, the Commission is empowered for purposes of physical
demarcation of a land boundary, to appoint official or licensed surveyors
or any other officer with their agents, servants and workmen to enter
land to demarcate or survey the land. This is to be undertaken in
accordance with the Lands Commission Act, 2008 (Act 767) and the Land
Act, 2020 (Act 1036). An officer or surveyor demarcating or surveying
boundaries may cause a notice to be served on any person owning,
occupying or otherwise interested in the abutting land or the land to be
surveyed, and on any person employed on or connected with the
management or cultivation of the land, requiring the person to attend or

iii

GHANA BOUNDARY COMMISSION BILL, 2023

be represented by an agent for deliberations on the demarcation at the
time and place stated in the notice. It is a criminal offence for a person to
willfully or unlawfully destroy, remove or alter a boundary post, to fail to
comply with an order in a notice served on that person, or willfully
obstruct, hinder or resist an authorised officer of the Commission in the
course of official duty of demarcating a boundary.

Clause 5 empowers an authorised officer to use firearms, in the
discharge of duties under the Bill or any other enactment.

The governance of the Commission is provided for in clauses 6 to 17.
The governing body of the Commission is a Board consisting of the
Minister responsible for Lands and Natural Resources as the chairperson
and the Ministers responsible for National Security, Interior, Defence,
Foreign Affairs and Energy. The other members are the Attorney-General
and Minister for Justice, representatives of Ministries responsible for
Finance, Local Government and Transport, the National House of Chiefs,
the Ghana Institution of Geoscientists, academia with expertise in
international security matters nominated by the Minister and the
Commissioner-General. The President is to, in accordance with article
70 of the Constitution, appoint the chairperson and other members of
the Board. The Board is to ensure the effective and efficient performance
of the functions of the Commission.

Standard provisions on duties and liabilities of a member of the
Board, tenure of office of members of the Board, meetings of the Board
and disclosure of interest are provided for in clauses 7, 8, 9 and 10
respectively.

The establishment of committees is provided for in clause 11. The
Board may establish committees consisting of members of the Board or
non-members or both to perform a function of the Board. In addition,
the Bill establishes the Land Boundary Technical Committee and the
Maritime Boundary Technical Committee. The provisions of clause 10
on disclosure of interest apply to members of a committee of the Board.

iv

GHANA BOUNDARY COMMISSION BILL, 2023

The membership of the Land Boundary Technical Committee
provided for under clause 12 include the Commissioner-General as the
chairperson and the Director of Surveys of the Lands Commission.
Representatives of the Ministries responsible for Lands and Natural
Resources, Justice, Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration, and National
Security are also members of the Committee. The Customs Division of
the Ghana Revenue Authority, the Immigration Service and the Ghana
Armed Forces are also represented. Two other persons nominated by the
Commission are also members of the Committee. The Land Boundary
Technical Committee is to meet at a time and place determined by the
chairperson.

Clause 13 provides for the functions of the Land Boundary Technical
Committee. The Land Boundary Technical Committee is to deal with
land boundary disputes with the view to settling the disputes, define land
boundaries with neighbouring countries and internal boundaries within
Ghana in accordance with the demarcation instrument or document,
proffer solutions to land boundary disputes and promote the development
and effective management of land boundaries. The Committee is also to
make recommendations to the Board on land boundary matters.

Clause 14 provides for the Maritime Boundary Technical Committee.
The membership of the Maritime Boundary Technical Committee
includes the Commissioner-General as the chairperson, representatives
of the Ghana Armed Forces, the Office of the Attorney-General and
Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration,
Petroleum Commission, the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation,
the Ghana Maritime Authority and the Ministry responsible for National
Security. The Director of the Survey and Mapping Division is also a
member of the Maritime Boundary Technical Committee. The
Commission is also to nominate two other persons as members of the
Commission. The time and place for the meetings of the Maritime
Boundary Technical Committee are to be determined by the chairperson
of the Committee.

GHANA BOUNDARY COMMISSION BILL, 2023

The functions of the Maritime Boundary Technical Committee are
provided for in clause 15. The Maritime Boundary Technical Committee
is responsible for dealing with matters affecting the maritime borders of
Ghana, participating in the delimitation of international maritime
boundaries in accordance with the delimitation instrument or documents
for that purpose, and proffering solutions to international maritime
boundary disputes. The Maritime Boundary Technical Committee is also
to promote trans-border cooperation and border area development and
make recommendations to the Board on international maritime boundary
matters.

Allowances for members of the Board and members of a committee
of the Board are provided for in clause 16. They are to be paid allowances
approved by the Minister in consultation with the Minister responsible
for Finance. The chairperson may give directives to the Board on matters
of policy and the Board is to comply, clause 17.

Clauses 18 to 25 provide for administrative matters. Departments of
the Commission are provided for in clause 18. The Commission is to
have a Boundaries Operations Department, Research Department, Survey
and Delimitation Department, Policy, Plans and Programmes
Department and an Administration Department. Nevertheless, the Board
may on the recommendation of the Commissioner-General realign the
Departments for the effective and efficient performance of the functions
of the Commission. A Department of the Commission is to be headed
by a Director.

Clause 19 enjoins the President to, in accordance with article 195 of
the Constitution, appoint a Commissioner-General for the Commission.
The Commissioner-General is to hold office on the terms and conditions
specified in the letter of appointment. The Commissioner-General is
responsible for the day-to-day administration of the affairs of the
Commission and is answerable to the Board in the performance of the
functions under the Bill, clause 20. The Commissioner-General may
however delegate a function to an officer of the Commission but is not
relieved of the ultimate responsibility for the performance of the delegated
function.

GHANA BOUNDARY COMMISSION BILL, 2023

Clause 21 enjoins the President to, in accordance with article 195 of
the Constitution, appoint a Deputy Commissioner-General. The Deputy
Commissioner-General is to hold office on the terms and conditions as
specified in the letter of appointment. The Deputy Commissioner-General
is to assist the Commissioner-General in the performance of the functions
of the Commissioner-General and to perform any other function as
assigned by the Commissioner-General.

The appointment of a Solicitor-Secretary is provided for in clause
22. The President is to in accordance with article 195 of the Constitution
appoint a Solicitor-Secretary for the Commission. The Solicitor-Secretary
is the secretary to the Board and the committees of the Board and is in
charge of the Legal Section of the Commission. The Solicitor-Secretary
is also responsible to the Commissioner-General in the performance of
functions.

Appointment of other staff by the President that are necessary for
the effective and efficient performance of the functions of the Commission
is provided for in clause 23. The appointments are to be done in accordance
with article 195 of the Constitution. In addition, the Commission may,
for the effective and efficient performance of the functions of the
Commission, engage the services of consultants and experts on the
recommendation of the Commissioner-General.

The Commission is to have an Internal Audit Unit in accordance
with section 83 of the Public Financial Management Act, 2016 (Act 921),
clause 24.

The Board may, on the recommendation of the Commissioner-
General, establish satellite regional offices of the Commission, clause 25.
A satellite regional office of the Commission is to perform functions of
the Commission in the region as the Board may direct.

Financial provisions are spelt out in clauses 26 to 30. The funds of the
Commission include moneys approved by Parliament, donations, grants,
gifts and internally generated funds, clause 26. Clause 27 provides for the 

vii

GHANA BOUNDARY COMMISSION BILL, 2023

moneys for the Commission to be paid into a bank account opened with
the approval of the Controller and Accountant-General. Under clause 28,
the expenses of the Commission sire to be a charge on the funds of the
Commission.

Standard provisions on accounts and audit, and annual report and
other reports are dealt with in clauses 29 and 30 respectively.

The last group of clauses, clauses 31 to 37 provide for miscellaneous
matters. The Commissioner-General, any other employee of the
Commission and a member of a committee of the Commission are
required to take the oath of office, oath of allegiance and the oath of
secrecy, before the commencement of functions under the Bill, clause 31.
In addition, subclause (2) of clause 31 enjoins, the Commissioner-General,
any other employee of the Commission and a committee of the
Commission to, on ceasing to be an employee or a member of a committee
of the Commission, be sworn out of office in accordance with the oath
provided for in the Schedule to the Bill.

Disclosure of information is dealt with in clause 32. An employee of
the Commission is not to disclose any information obtained in the
performance of a function under the Bill except as required by the Bill or
any other enactment. Despite the restriction, paragraphs (a), (b) and (c)
of subclause (2) provide for disclosure in certain circumstances including
the disclosure to a public officer who has authority to investigate an alleged
contravention of a law or to die Attorney-General, if the information is
required for an investigation or prosecution or disclosure to the Chief
Justice if the information is required by a court of competent jurisdiction.
A person who contravenes this clause commits an offence and is liable on
summary conviction to a fine or a term of imprisonment.

Collaboration with other bodies is provided for in clause 33. The
Commission is to collaborate with other relevant bodies in the performance
of functions under the Bill. Under clause 34, the Board may by legislative
instrument make Regulations to provide for the methodology to
demarcate a land boundary or delimit a maritime boundary, for the 

viii

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

keeping of records, reporting procedures and conditions of service of
staff of the Commission, among others.

Interpretation of some words and phrases used in the Bill is provided
for in clause 35. The Bill in clause 36 repeals the Ghana Boundary
Commission Act, 2010 (Act 795) and saves any Regulations, bye-laws,
notices, orders, directions, appointments or other acts lawfully made or
done under Act 795 and in force immediately before the coming into
force of the Bill until amended, revoked, cancelled, withdrawn or
terminated under the Bill.

Finally, transitional matters are dealt with in clause 37.

HON. SAMUEL A. JINAPOR, M.P.
Minister responsible for Lands and

Natural Resources

Date: 13th November, 2023.

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

BILL
ENTITLED

GHANA BOUNDARY COMMISSION ACT, 2023

AN ACT to establish the Ghana Boundary Commission to determine
and demarcate the land boundaries of Ghana and delimit the
maritime boundaries of Ghana in accordance with accepted
principles of international law, to protect and secure the interest of
the Republic in determining and demarcating land boundaries and
delimiting maritime boundaries of Ghana and to provide for
related matters.

PASSED by Parliament and assented to by the President:

The Ghana Boundary Commission
Establishment of the Ghana Boundary Commission

1. (1) There is established by this Act, the Ghana Boundary Commission
as a body corporate.

(2) For the performance of the functions of the Commission, the
Commission may acquire and hold property, dispose of property and
enter into a contract or any other related transaction.

3

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

(3) Where there is a hindrance to the acquisition of land, the land
may be acquired for the Commission under the Land Act, 2020 (Act 1036)
and the cost shall be borne by the Commission.
Objects of the Commission

2. The objects of the Commission are to
(a) in collaboration with the Lands Commission, undertake

negotiations to determine and demarcate land boundaries
of Ghana and delimit the maritime boundaries of Ghana
in accordance with accepted principles of international law;

(b) protect and secure the interest of the Republic in determining
and demarcating land boundaries and delimiting maritime
boundaries of Ghana;

(c) adopt international best practice in the demarcation of land
boundaries and delimiting of maritime boundaries of
Ghana;

(d) promote an effective and efficient management of the
boundary demarcation and delimitation processes; and

(e) ensure consideration of the interest of Ghanaians affected
by the placement of boundaries.

Functions of the Commission
3. To achieve the objects under section 2, the Commission shall

(a) negotiate with a neighbouring country concerning a land
boundary, maritime boundary or air boundary between
Ghana and that country;

(b) in collaboration with relevant security agencies, ensure the
security of the boundaries of Ghana to safeguard the
territorial sovereignty of Ghana at all times;

(c) in collaboration with the Lands Commission, undertake
the physical demarcation and survey of land boundaries
and the delimitation of maritime boundaries;

(d) whenever determined by the Board, place buoys or other
maritime markers along some or all of the courses of the
maritime boundaries of Ghana;

(e) advise Government on the most appropriate strategy for
the negotiation of a land boundary or maritime boundary;

(f) through negotiation, determine cross-boundary matters
among communities;

4

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

(g) encourage negotiated settlement of border disputes in
preference to litigation;

(h) intervene, determine or deal with a boundary dispute among
regions, districts or communities within Ghana with the
view to settling the dispute;

(i) promote trans-border cooperation and local community
development;

(j) advise Government on international Conventions in
relation to the borders of Ghana, and the signing and
ratification of treaties related to land and maritime boundaries;

(k) address issues related to the use of natural resources that
straddle land boundaries and maritime boundaries;

(I) formulate policies and implement programmes on intemational
boundaries including land boundaries and maritime
boundaries;

(m) coordinate with the relevant international body on
maritime demarcation across the international sea bed; and

(n) perform any other function ancillary to the objects of the
Commission.

Powers of the Commission and an Authorised Officer
Powers of the Commission

4. (1) In accordance with the Lands Commission Act, 2008 (Act 767)
and the Land Act, 2020 (Act 1036), the Commission may, for the
purpose of physical demarcation of a land boundary, appoint an official
surveyor, a licensed surveyor or any other officer with the agents,
servants and workmen of the official surveyor, licensed surveyor or other
officer to enter land to demarcate or survey the land.

(2) An officer or surveyor demarcating or surveying boundaries
may cause a notice to be served

(a) on any person owning, occupying or otherwise interested
in the abutting land or the land to be surveyed, and

(b) on any person employed on or connected with the
management or cultivation of the land,

requiring the person to attend or be represented by an agent for
deliberations on the demarcation or survey at the time and place stated
in the notice.

5

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

(3) An officer or surveyor may
(a) issue a notice calling on any person who is able to give

information on the boundaries of land in whose possession
or power any document related to the boundaries is alleged
to be, to meet the officer or surveyor and give information
or produce the document on the date and at a place
specified in the notice;

(b) place a boundary post in the manner prescribed in the
Technical Guidelines for Surveying and Mapping in Ghana
in the line of demarcation; and

(c) for the delimitation of a maritime boundary or demarcation
of a freshwater boundary,

(i) conduct hydrographic surveys in accordance with
international standards; and

(ii) create and manage a database of the hydrographic
surveys carried out on the maritime boundaries of
Ghana.

(4) A person who
(a) willfully or unlawfully destroys, removes or alters a boundary

post,
(b) fails to comply with an order in a notice served on that

person, or
(c) willfully obstructs, hinders or resists an authorised officer

of the Commission in the course of official duty to demarcate a
boundary,

commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not
less than two hundred penalty units and not more than five hundred penalty
units or to a term of imprisonment of not less than six months and not
more than three years or to both.

Power to use firearms
5. An authorised officer may, in the discharge of duties under this Act

or any other enactment, use firearms.

6

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

Governance of the Commission
Governing body of the Commission

6. (1) The governing body of the Commission is a Board consisting
of

(a) the Minister responsible for Lands and Natural Resources
as the chairperson;

(b) the Ministers responsible for the following:
(i) National Security;
(ii) Interior;
(iii) Defence;
(iv) Foreign Affairs; and
(v) Energy;

(c) the Attorney-General and Minister responsible for Justice;
(d) one representative of the following:

(i) the Ministry responsible for Finance not below the
rank of a Director nominated by the Minister
responsible for Finance;

(ii) the Ministry responsible for Local Government not
below the rank of a Director nominated by the
Minister responsible for Local Government;

(iii) the Ministry responsible for Transport not below the
rank of a Director nominated by the Minister
responsible for Transport;

(iv) the National House of Chiefs nominated by the
National House of Chiefs;

(v) the Ghana Institution of Geoscientists nominated
by the Ghana Institution of Geoscientists; and

(vi) academia with expertise in international security
matters nominated by the Minister; and

(e) the Commissioner-General.
(2) The President shall, in accordance with article 70 of the

Constitution, appoint the chairperson and other members of the Board.
(3) The Board shall ensure the efficient and effective performance

°f the functions of the Commission.

7

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

Duties and liabilities of a member of the Board
7. (1) A member of the Board has the same fiduciary relationship with

the Commission and the same duty to act with loyalty and in good faith
as a director of a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2019
(Act 992).

(2) Without limiting subsection (1), a member of the Board has a
duty to

(a) act honestly and in the best interest of the Commission in
the performance of the functions of that member;

(b) exercise the degree of care and diligence in the performance
of the functions of that member that a person in that
position would reasonably be expected to exercise in the
circumstance;

(c) avoid making use of information acquired by virtue of the
position of that member so as to benefit that member or to
the detriment of the Commission.

(3) A member of the Board who contravenes subsection (1) or (2)
commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not
less than one hundred penalty units and not more than two hundred and
fifty penalty units.
Tenure of office of members of the Board

8. (1) A member of the Board shall hold office for a term of four years
and is eligible for re-appointment for another term only.

(2) Subsection (1) does not apply to the Ministers of State specified
under paragraph (b) of subsection (1) of section 6, the Attorney-General
and Minister responsible for Justice and the Commissioner-General.

(3) A member of the Board may at any time resign from office in
writing addressed to the President through the chairperson of the Board.

(4) A member of the Board who is absent from three consecutive
meetings of the Board without sufficient cause ceases to be a member of
the Board.

(5) The President may, by a letter addressed to a member, revoke the
appointment of that member.

(6) Where a member of the Board is, for a sufficient reason, unable
to act as a member, the Minister shall determine whether the inability
would result in the declaration of a vacancy.

8

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

(7) Where there is a vacancy
(a) under subsection (3), (4), or (5), or subsection (2) of section

10,
(b) as a result of a declaration under subsection (6), or
(c) by reason of the death of a member,

the Minister shall notify the President of the vacancy and the President
shall appoint another person to fill the vacancy for the unexpired term.

Meetings of the members of the Board
9. (1) The members of the Board shall meet at least once every three

months for the conduct of business at a time and in a place determined
by the chairperson.

(2) The chairperson shall, at the request in writing of not less than
one-third of the membership of the Board, convene an extraordinary
meeting of the Board at a time and in a place determined by the
chairperson.

(3) The chairperson shall preside at meetings of the Board and in
the absence of the chairperson, a member of the Board, other than the
Commissioner-General, elected by the members present from among their
number shall preside.

(4) The quorum at a meeting of the Board is seven members and
shall include the Commissioner-General or the person acting in that
capacity.

(5) A matter before the Board shall be decided by a majority of the
members present and voting and in the event of an equality of votes, the
person presiding shall have a casting vote.

(6) The Board may co-opt a person to attend a meeting of the Board
but that person shall not vote on a matter for a decision at the meeting.

(7) The proceedings of the Board are not invalidated by reason of a
vacancy among the members of the Board or by a defect in the
appointment or the disqualification of a member.

(8) Subject to this Act, the Board shall regulate the procedure for
the meetings of the Board.

9

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

Disclosure of interest
10. (1) A member of the Board who has an interest in a matter for

consideration by the Board shall
(a) disclose in writing the nature of that interest and the

disclosure shall form part of the record of the consideration
of the matter; and

(b) be disqualified from being present at or participating in the
deliberations of the Board in respect of that matter.

(2) A member ceases to be a member of the Board, if that member
has an interest in a matter before the Board and

(a) fails to disclose that interest; or
(b) is present at or participates in the deliberations of the Board

in respect of that matter.
(3) Without limiting any further cause of action that may be

instituted against a member, the Commission shall recover any benefit
derived by a member who contravenes subsection (1), in addition to the
revocation of the appointment of the member.

(4) A member of the Board who fails to disclose an interest in a
matter for consideration by the Board is liable to pay compensation to
the Commission for any loss incurred.

Establishment of committees
11. (1) The Board may establish committees consisting of members

of the Board or non-members or both to perform a function of the Board.
(2) A committee of the Board consisting of members or

non-members or both may be chaired by a member of the Board.
(3) Without limiting subsection (1), there is established by this Act

(a) the Land Boundary Technical Committee; and
(b) the Maritime Boundary Technical Committee.

(4) Section 10 applies to members of a committee of the Board.

Land Boundary Technical Committee
12. (1) The Land Boundary Technical Committee consists of

(a) the Commissioner-General as chairperson;
(b) the Director of Surveys of the Lands Commission;

10

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

(c) one representative of the Attorney-General and Minister
responsible for Justice not below the rank of Chief State
Attorney;

(d) one representative of the following not below the rank of a
Director or its equivalent:

(i) Ministry responsible for Foreign Affairs and
Regional Integration nominated by the Minister
responsible for Foreign Affairs and Regional
Integration;

(ii) Ministry responsible for National Security
nominated by the Minister responsible for National
Security;

(iii) Ministry responsible for Lands and Natural
Resources nominated by the Minister responsible
for Lands and Natural Resources;

(iv) Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority
nominated by the Commissioner of the Customs
Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority;

(v) Immigration Service nominated by the Comptroller-
General of the Immigration Service; and

(vi) Ghana Armed Forces nominated by the Chief of
Defence Staff; and

(e) two other persons nominated by the Commission -
(2) The Land Boundary Technical Committee shall meet at a time

and place determined by the chairperson.
Functions of the Land Boundary Technical Committee

13. The Land Boundary Technical Committee shall
(a) deal with land boundary disputes with the view to settling

the dispute;
(b) detine land boundaries with a neighbouring country and

internal boundaries within Ghana in accordance with the
demarcation instrument or document for that purpose;

(c) proffer solutions to land boundary disputes;
(d) promote the development and effective management of land

boundaries; and
(e) make recommendations to the Board on land boundary

matters.

11

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

Maritime Boundary Technical Committee
14. (1) The Maritime Boundary Technical Committee consists of

(a) the Commissioner-General as chairperson;
(b) one representative each of the following not below the rank

of a Director:
(i) the Ministry responsible for Foreign Affairs and

Regional Integration nominated by the Minister
responsible for Foreign Affairs and Regional
Integration;

(ii) the Ministry responsible for National Security
nominated by the Minister responsible for National
Security;

(iii) the Petroleum Commission nominated by the Chief
Executive Officer of the Petroleum Commission;

(iv) the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation
nominated by the Chief Executive Officer of the
Ghana National Petroleum Corporation; and

(v) the Ghana Maritime Authority nominated by the
Director-General of the Ghana Maritime Authority;

(c) one representative of the Ghana Armed Forces not below
the rank of Colonel or an equivalent rank nominated by the
Chief of the Defence Staff;

(d) one representative of the Office of the Attorney-General
and Ministry of Justice not below the rank of Chief State
Attorney nominated by the Attorney-General and Minister
responsible for Justice;

(e) the Director of the Survey and Mapping Division; and
(f) two other persons nominated by the Commission.

(2) The Maritime Boundary Technical Committee shall meet at a
time and place determined by the chairperson of the Maritime Boundary
Technical Committee.

Functions of the Maritime Boundary Technical Committee
15. The Maritime Boundary Technical Committee shall

(a) deal with matters affecting the maritime borders of Ghana;

12

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

(b) participate in the delimitation of international maritime
boundaries in accordance with the delimitation instrument
or documents for that purpose;

(c) proffer solutions to international maritime boundary
disputes;

(d) promote trans-border cooperation and border area
development; and

(e) make recommendations to the Board on international
maritime boundary matters.

Allowances
16. Members of the Board and members of a committee of the Board

shall be paid allowances approved by the Minister in consultation with
the Minister responsible for Finance.

Policy directives
17. The chairperson may give directives to the Board on matters of

policy and the Board shall comply.

Administrative Provisions
Departments of the Commission

18. (1) The Commission shall have the following Departments:
(a) Boundary Operations Department;
(b) Research Department;
(c) Survey and Delimitation Department;
(d) Policy, Plans and Programmes Department; and
(e) Administration Department.

(2) Despite subsection (1), the Board may on the recommendation
of the Commissioner-General realign the Departments for the effective
and efficient performance of the functions of the Commission.

(3) A Department of the Commission shall be headed by a Director.

Appointment of Commissioner-General
19. (1) The President shall, in accordance with article 195 of the

Constitution, appoint a Commissioner-General for the Commission.

13

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

(2) A person is qualified to be appointed as a Commissioner if
that person

(a) has the relevant qualification, experience and expertise; and
(b) is of proven integrity.

(3) The Commissioner-General shall hold office on the terms and
conditions specified in the letter of appointment.
Functions of the Commissioner-General

20. (1) The Commissioner-General is
(a) responsible for the day-to-day administration of the affairs

of the Commission, and
(b) answerable to the Board in the performance of the

functions under this Act.
(2) The Commissioner-General may delegate a function to an

officer of the Commission but shall not be relieved of the ultimate
responsibility for the performance of the delegated function.
Appointment of Deputy Commissioner-General

21. (1) The President shall, in accordance with article 195 of the
Constitution, appoint a Deputy Commissioner-General.

(2) The Deputy Commissioner-General shall hold office on the
terms and conditions specified in the letter of appointment.

(3) The Deputy Commissioner-General shall
(a) assist the Commissioner-General in the performance of the

functions of the Commissioner-General; and
(b) perform any other function as assigned by the

Commissioner-General.
Appointment of Solicitor-Secretary

22. (1) The President shall, in accordance with article 195 of the
Constitution, appoint a person with expertise in international law as
Solicitor-Secretary for the Commission.

(2) The Solicitor-Secretary
(a) is the secretary to the Board and the committees of the

Board,
(b) is in charge of the Legal Section of the Commission,
(c) is responsible to the Commissioner-General in the

performance of functions; and
(d) shall perform the functions that the Board or the

Commissioner-General in consultation with the Board may
assign.

14

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

Appointment of other staff
23. (1) The President shall, in accordance with article 195 of the

Constitution, appoint other staff of the Commission that are necessary
for the effective and efficient performance of the functions of the
Commission.

(2) The Commission may, for the effective and efficient
performance of the functions of the Commission, engage the services of
consultants and experts on the recommendation of the Commissioner-
General.
Internal Audit Unit

24. (1) The Commission shall have an Internal Audit Unit in
accordance with section 83 of the Public Financial Management Act, 2016
(Act 921).

(2) The Internal Audit Unit shall be headed by an Internal
Auditor who shall be appointed in accordance with the Internal Audit
Agency Act, 2003 (Act 658).

(3) The Internal Auditor is responsible for the internal audit of
the Commission.

(4) The Internal Auditor shall, subject to subsections (3) and (4) of
section 16 of the Internal Audit Agency Act, 2003 (Act 658), at intervals
of three months

(a) prepare and submit to the Board, a report on the internal
audit carried out during the period of three months
immediately preceding the preparation of the report; and

(b) make recommendations in each report, with respect to
matters which appear to the Internal Auditor as necessary
for the conduct of the affairs of the Commission.

(5) The Internal Auditor shall, in accordance with subsection (4)
of section 16 of the Internal Audit Agency Act, 2003 (Act 658), submit a
copy of each report prepared under this section to the Commissioner-
General and the chairperson of the Commission.
Regional offices of the Commission

25. (1) The Board may, on the recommendation of the Commissioner-
General, establish satellite regional offices of the Commission.

(2) A satellite regional office of the Commission shall perform
functions of the Commission in the region as the Board may direct.

15

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

Financial Provisions
Funds of the Commission

26. The funds of the Commission include
(a) moneys approved by Parliament;
(b) donations, grants and gifts;
(c) internally generated funds; and
(d) any other moneys from public funds approved by the

Minister responsible for Finance.

Bank account of the Commission
27. The moneys for the Commission shall be paid into a bank

account opened with the approval of the Controller and Accountant-
General.

Expenses of the Commission
28. The expenses of the Commission shall be a charge on the funds of

the Commission.

Accounts and audit
29. (1) The Board shall keep books, records, returns of accounts and

other documents relevant to the accounts in the form approved by the
Auditor-General.

(2) The Board shall submit the accounts of the Commission to the
Auditor-General for audit at the end of the financial year.

(3) The Auditor-General shall, within six months after the end of
the immediately preceding financial year, audit the accounts and
forward a copy each of the audit report to the Minister and the Board.

(4) The financial year of the Commission is die same as the financial
year of Government.

Annual report and other reports
30. (1) The Board shall, within thirty days after the receipt of the audit

report, submit an annual report to the Minister covering the activities
and operations of the Commission for the year to which the annual
report relates.

(2) The annual report shall include the report of the Auditor-General.

16

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

(3) The Minister shall, within thirty days after the receipt of the
annual report, submit the report to Parliament with a statement that the
Minister considers necessary.

(4) The Board shall also submit to the Minister any other report
which the Minister may require in writing.

Miscellaneous Provisions

Oaths
31. (1) The Commissioner-General, any other employee of the

Commission and a member of a committee of the Commission shall,
before the commencement of functions under this Act, take the oath of
office, oath of allegiance and the oath of secrecy, as provided in the Schedule.

(2) The Commissioner-General, any other employee of the
Commission and a committee of the Commission shall, on ceasing to be
an employee or a member of a committee of the Commission be sworn
out of office in accordance with the oath, as provided in the Schedule.

Disclosure of information
32. (1) An employee of the Commission shall not disclose any

information obtained in the performance of a function under this Act
except as required by this Act or any other enactment.

(2) Despite subsection (1), the Commission may permit the
disclosure of information by an employee under this Act

(a) to a public officer who has authority to investigate an
alleged contravention of a law or to the Attorney-General,
if the information is required for an investigation or
prosecution;

(b) to the Chief Justice, if the information is required by a court
of competent jurisdiction; or

(c) to a Minister of State or person in the public service, if in
the opinion of the Commissioner-General the disclosure
of the information is essential in the public interest, and
the public interest outweighs an invasion of privacy that
may result from the disclosure.

17

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

(3) A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence
and is liable on summary conviction to a term of imprisonment of not
less than five years and not more than ten years.

Collaboration with other bodies
33. The Commission shall collaborate with other relevant bodies in

the performance of functions under this Act.

Regulations
34. (1) The Board may by legislative instrument make Regulations to

(a) provide for the methodology to demarcate a land boundary
or delimit a maritime boundary;

(b) for the keeping of records;
(c) reporting procedures;
(d) conditions of service of staff of the Commission;
(e) prescribe for discipline of staff of the Commission; and
(f) provide for any other matter necessary for the effective and

efficient implementation of provisions of this Act.
(2) The Commission may impose administrative penalties for a

contravention of paragraphs (b) and (c) of subregulation (1).

Interpretation
35. Tn this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,

“authorised officer” means an officer designated in writing as
having the authority to act on behalf of the Commission;

“Board” means the governing body of the Commission
established under section 6;

“border area development” means a special development which
addresses the needs and well-being of people living in
remote and inaccessible areas near a maritime boundary;

“boundary” means national or international boundary;
“boundary post” means a pillar or a monument placed on land

as a signal or guide to a boundary;
“buoy” means an anchored float serving as a navigation mark;
“Commission” means the Ghana Boundary Commission

established under section 1;

18

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

“Commissioner-General” means the person appointed under
section 19;

“local community development” means the process where a
community or members of the community are supported
to identify and take action on issues which are important
for the improvement of the community;

“freshwater boundary” means a naturally occurring water,
except seawater and brackish water, which is used as a boundary;

“land boundary” means the extent of legal limits of ownership
of a parcel of land;

“maritime boundary” means the extent of legal limits of
ownership of maritime waters and resources to include the
Exclusive Economic Zone and the Extended Continental
Shelf;

“Minister” means the Minister responsible for Lands and
Natural Resources;

“relevant bodies” means bodies or agencies that have the
responsibility to provide services or collaborate with the
Commission in the performance of functions under this
Act;

“Technical Guidelines for Surveying and Mapping in Ghana”
means a reference document used to specify how surveying
and mapping is carried out on land in Ghana; and

“trans-border cooperation” means collaboration between
adjacent areas, communities and the people across the
international boundary.

Repeal and savings
36. (1) The Ghana Boundary Commission Act, 2010 (Act 795) is

repealed.
(2) Despite the repeal of Act 795, any Regulations, bye-laws,

notices, orders, directions, appointments or other acts lawfully made or
done under the repealed enactment and in force immediately before the
coming into force of this Act shall, continue to have effect as if made
under this Act with the necessary modification until amended, revoked,
cancelled, withdrawn or terminated under this Act.

19

Ghana Boundary Commission Bill, 2023

Transitional provisions
37. (1) The assets, rights and properties held on behalf of or for the

purpose of the Commission in existence immediately before the coming
into force of this Act and the persons employed by the Commission are
transferred to the Commission established under this Act.

(2) The obligations and liabilities subsisting against the Commission
immediately before the coming into force of this Act subsist between the
Commission established under this Act and that other party.
